A late result must execute the ordinary resolution and activation sequence before joining 𝐴𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑣𝑒\mathit{Active}. Therefore every non-activation transition preserves all six invariants. ∎

Lemma 0 (Fault steps preserve safety).

If I1–I6 hold before a crash, they hold in 𝖢𝗋𝖺𝗌𝗁⁡(s)\mathsf{Crash}(s) and throughout every finite recovery prefix in 𝖱𝖾𝖼𝗈𝗏𝖾𝗋⁡(s)\mathsf{Recover}(s). The slot bounds of Lemma 5 also hold throughout.

Proof.

By A6, 𝖢𝗋𝖺𝗌𝗁⁡(s)\mathsf{Crash}(s) is the state after the last fully committed transaction, hence a committed prefix of the pre-crash execution rather than a partial authority-changing write. I1–I6 held at that prefix by the ordinary transition lemmas. Every recovery action is an ordinary guarded transition in ℛ\mathcal{R}: Lemma 8 covers a successful activation transaction and Lemma 9 covers the remaining actions. Induction over the finite recovery prefix preserves I1–I6. Lemma 5 separately supplies the slot bounds across both the crash projection and those transactions. In particular, a crash before an effect commit’s A10 linearization point exposes neither acceptance nor its durable receipt and used-slot row; a crash after that point exposes the complete committed set. Recovery cannot create a second acceptance for the same effect slot. ∎

Theorem 11 (Invariant preservation).

Under A1–A11, I1–I6 hold after every prefix of every fault-extended accepted trace.

Proof.

By induction on trace length. Lemma 6 is the base case. Lemma 8 handles a successful activation step, and Lemma 9 handles every other accepted ordinary transition. Lemma 10 handles crashes and finite recovery prefixes. ∎

A.2. Separation propositions

Proof of Proposition 11.

Assume for contradiction that a function f⁡(z)f(z) is sound and complete for activation. Let provider worlds w1,w2w_{1},w_{2} produce the same transaction tuple zz, but resolve to α1,α2\alpha_{1},\alpha_{2}, inducing candidate edges e1,e2e_{1},e_{2} with ΦΓ(H⊞ρ⁡(Γ)({e1}∪𝗈𝗎𝗍(e1)))=𝗍𝗋𝗎𝖾\Phi_{\Gamma}(H\boxplus_{\rho(\Gamma)}(\{e_{1}\}\cup\mathsf{out}(e_{1})))=\mathsf{true} and ΦΓ(H⊞ρ⁡(Γ)({e2}∪𝗈𝗎𝗍(e2)))=𝖿𝖺𝗅𝗌𝖾\Phi_{\Gamma}(H\boxplus_{\rho(\Gamma)}(\{e_{2}\}\cup\mathsf{out}(e_{2})))=\mathsf{false}. Because its input is equal, ff returns the same result in both worlds. If that result accepts, it is unsound in w2w_{2}; every non-accepting result, including indeterminate, is incomplete in w1w_{1}. Contradiction. An authenticated actual-output observation or a sound profile upper bound is therefore necessary to distinguish the worlds. ∎

Proof of Proposition 12.

Fix one canonical control root 𝑐𝑟\mathit{cr} and two descriptors αr\alpha_{r} and αp\alpha_{p} containing, respectively, a sensitive-read and an external-publish episode. Let ΦΓ​(H)\Phi_{\Gamma}(H) hold exactly when HH does not contain both capabilities controlled by 𝑐𝑟\mathit{cr}. This predicate is downward closed. Its component allowlists contain 𝑐𝑟\mathit{cr}, both effect classes, both targets, and all other individual fields, so a componentwise membership test accepts each descriptor and their field union. Yet the graph containing both makes ΦΓ\Phi_{\Gamma} false. Hence componentwise checks do not preserve the correlation. ∎

Proof of Proposition 13.

Let the monetary invariant be total spend at most B>0B>0, and let ΦΓ\Phi_{\Gamma} permit at most one active descendant for 𝑐𝑟\mathit{cr}. Two zero-price enrollment operations preserve total spend 0≤B0\leq B. If both outputs activate, the descendant count is two and ΦΓ\Phi_{\Gamma} is false. Thus monetary compliance does not imply acquisition safety. The same construction applies to prohibited co-possession. ∎

A.3. Safety theorem proofs

Proof of Theorem 14.

Lemma 7 enumerates every pre-commit transition and shows that none writes active authority or publishes a handle. A1 ensures no registered acquisition or effect path bypasses these transitions; A3 prevents resolution from manufacturing a silent grant; A6 orders the durable active record before publication; and A10 requires a broker-accepted handle for a protected effect. Therefore only a successful 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗆𝗂𝗍𝖠𝖼𝗍𝗂𝗏𝖺𝗍𝗂𝗈𝗇\mathsf{CommitActivation} creates active authority, and executability arises only when the broker subsequently publishes a handle for that durable active record. ∎

Proof of Theorem 15.

Consider executable xx. By the definition of 𝖤𝗑𝖾𝖼s\mathsf{Exec}_{s}, it has a unique matching active row aa; set Γ=𝗋𝗈𝗈𝗍⁡(a)\Gamma=\mathsf{root}(a). By I2 the row has a committed activation edge. Invariant preservation gives I3 directly: the row has a current acyclic derivation whose unique provenance root is the live Γ\Gamma. Finiteness and acyclicity make recursive traversal terminate at a source or capability seed authorized by that root. Because the base transition system rejects cross-root capability combinations, every traversed edge retains the same root. Hence the derivation terminates at exactly one live root 𝑔𝑖𝑑\mathit{gid} under the profile’s root-identity rule. This provenance uniqueness does not create a separate accounting compartment: I5 still evaluates the union of all live roots in that root’s authority domain. ∎

Proof of Theorem 16.

Theorem 11 gives, for every live authority domain ρ\rho, 𝖲𝖺𝖿𝖾ρ​(s,Πρ​(s))\mathsf{Safe}_{\rho}(s,\Pi_{\rho}(s)) in every reachable state. This is the relational non-amplification statement, including the case in which the domain contains several provenance 𝑔𝑖𝑑\mathit{gid} values. For the root-specific episode-set corollary, every x∈𝖠𝖼𝗍𝗂𝗏𝖾Γ​(s)x\in\mathsf{Active}_{\Gamma}(s) lies on a valid current path from Γ\Gamma by Theorem 15. I4 supplies κe∈KΓ\kappa_{e}\in K_{\Gamma}, ωe∈Ωκe\omega_{e}\in\Omega_{\kappa_{e}}, well-typed input/output tuples, RκeR_{\kappa_{e}}, and the registered ordinal-specific per-edge bound. The source leaves belong to 𝖡𝖺𝗌𝖾Γ\mathsf{Base}_{\Gamma}. Induction on path length, with every input tuple’s components already reachable, applies the Step rule defining 𝖱𝖾𝖺𝖼𝗁Γ\mathsf{Reach}_{\Gamma}, so every such xx belongs to that least set and [[αx]]⊆𝖢𝗅Γ\mathopen{[\![}\alpha_{x}\mathclose{]\!]}\subseteq\mathsf{Cl}_{\Gamma} by definition. Unioning these inclusions proves the displayed subset. The main I5 statement remains strictly stronger because the conjunction over 𝖫𝗂𝗏𝖾ρ​(s)\mathsf{Live}_{\rho}(s) also constrains identities, counts, co-possession, and topology across sibling grant identifiers. ∎

Proof of Theorem 17.

By Definition 7, normalization removes precisely the syntactic distinctions allowed by the theorem and retains every semantic output, canonical identity, count, relation, and edge. Equal normalized additions therefore present identical shared-domain projections to every predicate in 𝖫𝗂𝗏𝖾ρ​(s)\mathsf{Live}_{\rho}(s), so the deterministic conjunction 𝖲𝖺𝖿𝖾ρ\mathsf{Safe}_{\rho} gives equal values. In particular, placing a second worker under a fresh sibling 𝑔𝑖𝑑\mathit{gid} does not hide it: both workers remain in Πρ\Pi_{\rho}, and a domain clause allowing at most one active worker rejects the second activation.

For the execution claim, fix an interval in which the live-grant set is unchanged and no exogenous transition removes authority from the projection, and suppose an interleaving fully activates a Δ\Delta for which 𝖲𝖺𝖿𝖾ρ(s,H⊞ρΔ)\mathsf{Safe}_{\rho}(s,H\boxplus_{\rho}\Delta) is false. Let eje_{j} be the final fragment commit and s−s^{-} its pre-state. Earlier fragments may have advanced the domain revision, so eje_{j} must have been prepared again or revalidated against that current revision. Because no authority was removed, Πρ+​(s−,ej)\Pi^{+}_{\rho}(s^{-},e_{j}) contains the normalized initial HH, all of Δ\Delta, and possibly additional authority. Downward closure gives the contrapositive: since the smaller H⊞ρΔH\boxplus_{\rho}\Delta is unsafe, this candidate extension is also unsafe. The commit guard therefore rejects eje_{j}, contradicting successful full activation. A safe prefix may remain active, which is consistent with non-evasion. If an accepted time, epoch, grant-currentness, fence, or destruction transition intervenes, it advances the domain revision and atomically refreshes the projection. No stale permit can cross that step. The argument then restarts from the new refresh-closed projection and live-grant set, so no unsafe intermediate aggregate is exposed. ∎

Proof of Theorem 18.

Consider an arbitrary state ss of an arbitrary fault-extended accepted trace and an arbitrary executable instance xx in that state. By the exact execution definition there is a unique row aa satisfying 𝖢𝗎𝗋𝗋𝖾𝗇𝗍𝖱𝗈𝗐s​(a,x)\mathsf{CurrentRow}_{s}(a,x) and the handle and active-coordinate guards; put j=𝗌𝗅𝗈𝗍⁡(a)j=\mathsf{slot}(a) and Γ=𝗋𝗈𝗈𝗍⁡(a)\Gamma=\mathsf{root}(a). Lemma 5 gives at most one durable active row for jj before any fault and preserves that bound through every crash and finite recovery prefix. More explicitly, a crash before the activation transaction’s linearization point projects to a state containing none of its writes. A crash after that point retains its complete write set, including the consumed slot and active row. There is no durable state containing only one of those two rows. Handle publication occurs only from the committed row. If recovery repeats publication, determinism yields the same handle rather than a second authority.

A replayed activation permit addresses the same slot, so its conflicting transaction aborts under 𝖴𝖭𝖨𝖰𝖴𝖤⁡(𝑠𝑙𝑜𝑡)\mathsf{UNIQUE}(\mathit{slot}). A duplicate receipt correlates with the existing logical operation and remains quarantined unless it passes a separate ordinary activation under the complete graph. A late success follows the same rule. Revalidation within any successful activation commit establishes the current manifest, live root, descriptor validity, epochs, and 𝖲𝖺𝖿𝖾ρ⁡(Γ)​(s,Πρ⁡(Γ)​(s))\mathsf{Safe}_{\rho(\Gamma)}(s,\Pi_{\rho(\Gamma)}(s)); each accepted time or epoch transition refreshes them before its post-state is observable. Theorem 11 preserves these facts across the fault-extended trace. Consequently every executable handle is backed by the unique safe committed active record for its slot, and no slot produces two simultaneously executable authorities. This is an at-most-once safety result: it does not assert that retries terminate or that any attempted activation eventually commits. A later epoch advance may leave a historical handle reference recorded while making 𝖤𝗑𝖾𝖼s​(x)\mathsf{Exec}_{s}(x) false, which is consistent with the theorem’s current-state antecedent. Since the used-slot row and active row co-commit, 𝖲𝗅𝗈𝗍𝖢𝗈𝗇𝗌𝗎𝗆𝖾𝖽s​(a)\mathsf{SlotConsumed}_{s}(a) also holds, proving every conjunct in the theorem’s implication. ∎

Proof of Theorem 19.

By definition, refund changes only Cs​(o)C_{s}(o) to Cs′​(o)=refundedC_{s^{\prime}}(o)=\text{refunded} and updates source evidence. It does not change any Ds​(o,ω)D_{s}(o,\omega), any slot-level As​(j)A_{s}(j), active row, or graph edge. Thus Πρ​(s′)=Πρ​(s)\Pi_{\rho}(s^{\prime})=\Pi_{\rho}(s) for every authority domain ρ\rho, and every domain capacity clause has the same value immediately before and after the refund. A later candidate is evaluated with the first capability still present unless a separate authorized transition occurs under the registered profile. Concretely, the old capability must be fenced (optionally followed by ordinary activation under a narrower descriptor) or verified as destroyed. Source restoration is not evidence that either event occurred. Hence restored money cannot resurrect a semantic slot by itself. ∎

Proof of Theorem 20.

Activation permits, active records, and effect permits bind the complete epoch vector; effect permits also bind the current domain revision. Activation commit, effect preparation, and effect commit compare these values with authoritative state. After any bound epoch advances, exact equality fails: an old activation permit cannot commit, an old effect permit cannot linearize an effect, and an old handle cannot obtain a current replacement permit. An authority-domain change likewise advances its revision and invalidates a prepared effect permit. Re-resolution and new activation are the only transitions that can bind a changed resource to the new epoch vector. ∎

Proof of Theorem 21.

Let rr and pup_{u} witness 𝖠𝖼𝖼𝖾𝗉𝗍𝖾𝖽𝖤𝖿𝖿𝖾𝖼𝗍sk+1​(x,u)\mathsf{AcceptedEffect}_{s_{k+1}}(x,u), with rr first appearing in sk+1s_{k+1}. By A1, A10, and I6, there is exactly one transition sk→𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗆𝗂𝗍𝖤𝖿𝖿𝖾𝖼𝗍⁡(pu)sk+1s_{k}\xrightarrow{\mathsf{CommitEffect}(p_{u})}s_{k+1} that atomically accepts the effect and appends rr and its previously unused effect-slot row. In the pre-state sks_{k}, the broker resolves the handle to the exact durable row aa and instance xx, with ρ=ρ⁡(𝗋𝗈𝗈𝗍⁡(a))\rho=\rho(\mathsf{root}(a)) and 𝐻𝑎𝑛𝑑𝑙𝑒𝑠sk​(χ)=a\mathit{Handles}_{s_{k}}(\chi)=a, Ask​(𝗌𝗅𝗈𝗍​(a))=activeA_{s_{k}}(\mathsf{slot}(a))=\text{active}, and 𝖢𝗎𝗋𝗋𝖾𝗇𝗍𝖱𝗈𝗐sk​(a,x)\mathsf{CurrentRow}_{s_{k}}(a,x). I6 also gives 𝖤𝗑𝖾𝖼sk​(x)\mathsf{Exec}_{s_{k}}(x). By Theorem 15, the row has a complete current derivation there. The guard compares the complete normalized episode, row root, authority domain, target-to-domain map commitment, epoch vector, and domain revision with pup_{u}, requires 𝗇𝗈𝗐⁡(sk)<𝖾𝗑𝗉𝗂𝗋𝗒⁡(pu)\mathsf{now}(s_{k})<\mathsf{expiry}(p_{u}), and checks u∈[[αx]]u\in\mathopen{[\![}\alpha_{x}\mathclose{]\!]}, 𝖤𝗉𝗂𝗌𝗈𝖽𝖾𝖢𝗎𝗋𝗋𝖾𝗇𝗍sk​(u)\mathsf{EpisodeCurrent}_{s_{k}}(u), 𝖮𝖻𝗅sk​(oαx,u)\mathsf{Obl}_{s_{k}}(o_{\alpha_{x}},u), and 𝖲𝖺𝖿𝖾ρ​(sk,Πρ​(sk))\mathsf{Safe}_{\rho}(s_{k},\Pi_{\rho}(s_{k})).

If the episode, handle, or active record was substituted after preparation, exact permit equality fails. If activation, fencing, destruction, grant issuance, or an epoch change intervened, the epoch or domain-revision check fails. If the same logical effect is replayed, the used-slot check fails. By A10 each failure aborts before the protected effect, whereas success appends the slot-consumption row atomically with effect acceptance. Consequently an accepted effect lies within the actual capability and current shared-domain envelope and cannot be detached from its acquisition provenance by a prepare-to-commit race. ∎
